newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops pound Tamil rebels in new assault.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops pound Tamil rebels in new assault.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces pounded Tamil Tiger positions on Monday in the government's latest bid to break into the rebels' northern stronghold but met heavy resistance, military officials said.
At least 30 government soldiers had been killed in the offensive, the officials said.
"The army is spreading out from their last-held positions," an official told Reuters. "We're meeting heavy resistance. About 50 soldiers have been wounded."
Troops who had consolidated positions around the northern road juction town of Paranthan launched the fresh push toward Kilinochchi on Sunday after a lull of more than a month.
It was not immediately clear if the 30 dead included 11 soldiers killed on Sunday.
"We heard reports of heavy shelling starting on Saturday night and going on till Sunday morning," a United Nations official in the northern town of Vavuniya told Reuters.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, accused the troops of attacking civilians.
"The armed forces are directing their attack on civilian concentrations which are scattered around the intended path of the army's advance," it said in a statement.
"From early in the morning air force bombers are flying regular sorties, bombing civilian concentrations and attacking fleeing civilians," it said.
Most of an estimated 150,000 people in Kilinochchi had evacuated the town since the military first launched its offensive in July but many lived on the outskirts of the town.
On the first day of the new offensive, soldiers at Elephant Pass at the neck of the northern Jaffna peninsula poured onto Paranthan to reinforce attack forces.
The Tigers set up positions at Kilinochchi, entry point to their jungle territory of Wanni, earlier this year after the army recaptured Jaffna peninsula.
The rebels had ruled the peninsula for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.

Despite security forces' air strikes and shelling from tanks and artillery, the rebels fought back using mortars, rockets and automatic rifles, killing the 11 soldiers and wounding many others, including a lieutenant colonel in the Armoured Corps.
The extent of rebel casualties was not immediately known but a military officer said: "The LTTE must have suffered heavy casualties because of air and artillery strikes."
Jaffna is now separated from the mainland by a big chunk of rebel-held territory that reaches from Kilinochchi to Vavuniya, 70 km (44 miles) south of the town.
The army has said it wants to reopen the main highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo which passes through rebel-controlled Wanni.
Opening the road would let the military supply the Jaffna peninsula more easily and cheaply than the aircraft and ships it now uses.
The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.
It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war and the army launched an offensive soon afterwards but its southward advance from Jaffna had been stalled near Kilinochchi.
Diplomats said there had been a lull in the war recently partly because the army had exhausted itself after a thrust towards Kilinochchi in July.
They said about 30 percent of the military's strength of 100,000 troops were held in Jaffna since its recapture of the peninsula last April to maintain security there.
